To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sulphide intrusion into eelgrass rhizeomes can be induced by oxygen depletion in the water column, that internal oxygen concentration is a key determinant for sulphide intrusion into the tissues of the seagrass, that sulphide intrusion can occur at oxygen concentrations that are not lethal to the seagrass and that the sulphide pool within the tissues is slowly depleted when internal oxygen concentration is reestablished.

1) sulphide intrusion into eelgrass rhizes and meristematic tissue can be induced, 2) sulphide intrusion is dependent on low internal oxygen concentrations, and 3) sulphide intrusion can be lethal to eelgrass.

(i) sulphide intrusion in eglrass tissues can be triggered by oxygen stress, (ii) the rate of sulphide intrusion is determined by oxygen concentrations in the eelgras tissues and (iii) the sulphide intrusion is reversible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the phytotoxic gas sulphide in the decline and death of eelgrass beds.
the role of oxygen and sulphide in seagrasses and their environment.

the following topics: (1) The role of the seagrass root system in oxygen supply and nutrient uptake; (2) The effects of oxygen stress on seagrass growth, survival and sulphide intrusion in seagrass tissue; (3) The effects of sulphide intrusion on photosynthetic performance, growth and survival in seagrass; (4) The effects of environmental stress on the seagrass‐bacteria interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sulphide intrusion in eulgrass can be induced by oxygen stress and that the resulting sulphide content can be high enough to induce seagrass mortality.
sulphide intrusion into eelgrass tissue is a consequence of oxygen stress, which may be induced by environmental factors such as low light and low temperature.

sulphide intrusion is not a general problem in healthy seagrass meadows but can be induced by low water column oxygen concentrations and that it may be the ultimate factor leading to sudden seagrass death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sulphide intrusion in Zostera marin a is a consequence of oxygen stress and that the internal oxygen status of the plant determines the extent of sulphide intrusion.
the oxygen supply to seagrass tissues is a critical factor in the sulphide intrusion process.
sulphide intrusion is a common feature of eelgrass and that the extent of the intrusion depends on the oxygen supply in eelgrass tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sulphide intrusion into eelgrass tissues is controlled by the plant oxygen status and that sulphide intrusion is likely to occur in seagrasses under oxygen stress, but not under high oxygen supply in the water column.
sulphide intrusion in seagrass is not a slow, continuous process, but rather a fast and sudden event.
sulphide intrusion can occur at low oxygen partial pressures ( < 2% of air saturation), which are common during eutrophication of coastal areas.
